title: Ericsson and LG Uplus validate Packet Fronthaul and automation on the path to AI RAN
summary: Ericsson and LG Uplus have completed a joint trial demonstrating how mobile networks can evolve toward AI RAN with greater flexibility, resilience and automation
body_markdown:
Ericsson (NASDAQ: ERIC)


and LG Uplus have completed a joint trial demonstrating how mobile networks can evolve toward AI RAN with greater flexibility, resilience and automation – while maximizing the value of existing infrastructure. By validating extended fronthaul reach, integrated network management and automatic failover, the trial provides a practical blueprint for communications service providers (CSPs) preparing for increasingly distributed and AI-native networks.


The trial demonstrated how


CSPs


can evolve their fronthaul architecture to


extend reach


, integrate existing and next-generation radio equipment, and reduce manual intervention in network operations. Fronthaul


provides


the


connectivity between


radio


units


and


RAN Compute, including


distributed


units (DUs


), and is


a key enabler of


flexible RAN deployments.


During the trial, LG Uplus integrated Ericsson’s Packet Fronthaul solution with its RAN equipment and evaluated multiple network configurations. The validation


covered interoperability with


existing and next-generation radio equipment,


demonstrating


a practical evolution path that maximizes the value of installed network assets while preparing


the network


for future architectures.


The trial also evaluated network automation and


the


integrated monitoring of RAN and transport


domains


through Ericsson Network Manager. Together with Packet Fronthaul, these capabilities


provide


a more unified operational view and can help


CSPs


simplify operations as networks become


increasingly


distributed and complex.


The joint validation showed the potential to extend the distance between


radio and RAN Compute


equipment while maintaining stable


network


performance. Ericsson and LG Uplus also tested DU redundancy, including automatic switchover from a failed DU to a standby DU.


This capability can strengthen


network resilience and


reduce


the need for manual intervention


in


network operations.


“Packet Fronthaul and network automation provide a practical


path for communications


service providers to evolve their RAN with greater flexibility, resilience and operational efficiency, while continuing to leverage existing


network


assets,” said Jaimie Jihyun Lee, Head of Networks Solutions Korea, Ericsson. “Together with LG Uplus, we have demonstrated how extended fronthaul


reach


and DU redundancy can support more integrated and automated


network


operations.


“In addition, as the industry moves toward AI-native networks, Ericsson will continue to


use


the right AI model in the right place


with the right compute, supported


by AI-ready


,


energy-efficient


infrastructure


, to help


service providers


prepare for future network requirements and services, including Physical AI.”


Sangheon Lee, Head of Advanced Network Development at LG Uplus, said: “This joint trial with Ericsson is


significant


because it validated key technologies for future network environments. We will continue


collaborating


with Ericsson to further evolve the fronthaul


capabilities needed for


AI RAN and next-generation networks.”


Ericsson’s AI RAN strategy brings together AI for networks and networks for AI. Intelligence is embedded across


radios


,


RAN Compute and the management


and orchestration layer, applying the right AI model in the right place with the right compute. This distributed, full-stack approach enables real-time optimization, improves performance and energy efficiency, and gives communications service providers


a scalable path toward


high-performing, programmable and


AI-native networks.


Building on the


trial


results, Ericsson and LG Uplus will continue to explore and evolve next-generation fronthaul and automation technologies.


The


collaboration supports the evolution


of


5G Standalone toward


5G Advanced and, over time, AI-native


6G


by strengthening the high-performing, resilient and energy-efficient connectivity foundation needed for


new


AI-powered services, including applications that require consistently


low


latency


and high reliability


.
